evidence.observed: silent deadlock (killed at 10s): the 16-hex id resolves to nothing without the mint's keyset list and the resolver deadlocks instead of erroring — wallet-state-dependent

decode.notes: cdk-cli's verdict on this shape is wallet-state-dependent: a warm wallet (mint keysets cached) decodes; a cold wallet hangs. The verdict records the reference-configuration (warm) answer; the cold-wallet hang is the documented failure mode and runners must apply timeouts. Contrast with the Go backend, which resolves the prefix and ACCEPTS (1022), and the portal pin, which rejects — the consumer spread on this one shape is the divergence the corpus exists to expose.

evidence.ref: corpus v0: backend accepts BOTH id spellings (1022); portal CU109 rejects every V2-era spelling

verify.notes: The shape that hid the portal defect for months: a test minter adopted this 'v2-short' truncation (exists nowhere in NUT-00/02) and the internally-consistent pair passed tests while real mints rotated to V2.

evidence.observed: proof (amount 4, secret matching the canonical keyset's Y) state=SPENT

checkstate.notes: The proofs were spent at the mint during the v0 verification run even though the token's id field is the truncated form: the swap request that reached the mint must have carried the canonical id, so the backend resolves the 16-hex prefix to the canonical V2 keyset id before swapping. The v4_v2_valid vector explains why this resolution exists: CDK's V4 serialization natively writes the 8-byte id prefix, so every V4-capable consumer already needs short-id resolution — the 'v2-short' spelling a test minter adopted (PRTA#247) is this native V4 form transplanted into V3.

evidence.ref: corpus v0 (PR #29) live verification against the rig

spend.notes: Consumers MUST NOT treat the 16-hex truncation of a V2 id as a distinct keyset: it is either resolved to the canonical id (backend behavior) or rejected (portal behavior). Silently minting NEW tokens with truncated ids (the test-minter regression) is forbidden — that is how the ecosystem invented a third id spelling.

provenance.minted_by: cdk-cli 0.18.0, then each proof id replaced by id[:16] and re-encoded (corpus v0, PR #29)
provenance.regen: decode the V3 token, set each proof id to the first 16 hex chars of the canonical id, re-encode
